target.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repair validation could prove one checkout state and later publish a mutable
`HEAD`, while target-controlled Git state, ignored runtime inputs, or surviving
child processes could influence later credential-bearing publication.

## Current Design

- publishes only the immutable validated commit SHA through isolated Git and
  explicit destination leases
- runs validation in a disposable Linux user/PID namespace
- restricts filesystem content and namespace writes to the target checkout and
  disposable profile/runtime roots with Landlock
- recursively binds resolved ignored-runtime symlink contents into the runtime
  identity
- reaps every remaining process in the private PID namespace, including
  detached double forks
- preserves hook-free Git plumbing and isolated authentication

The configurable repair runner contract now requires Linux, delegated user
namespaces, and Landlock ABI 3 or newer.

## Exact-Head Evidence

Head: `85dc532697207ce38ddbcd9a79f38337026d6025`

- GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29338485217
  - `pnpm check`: 2,012 tests, 2,008 passed, 4 platform skips, 0 failed
  - Windows launcher and crawl integration passed
- CodeQL: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29338485464
  - actions and JavaScript/TypeScript analyses passed
- hosted Linux proof: Crabbox AWS lease `cbx_4e8eb72043ab`, run
  `run_58e9e9a94fd5`
  - exact pushed head confirmed
  - private namespace PID 1 and Landlock ABI 8 confirmed
  - filesystem write-root regression passed without skips
  - namespace-init cleanup regression passed without skips
  - ignored external runtime symlink mutation regression passed without skips
  - immediate detached double-fork regression passed without skips
- both TypeScript builds, focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, Actionlint 1.7.12,
  and `git diff --check` passed locally
- release-owned `CHANGELOG.md` remains untouched

## Exact Review Status

A fresh local-only ClawSweeper review completed against
`main` `ecc6d03d1ec73267d434cb1905cfc216c78fcd70` and this exact head. It returned
`keep_open` with high confidence.

The ignored external symlink target finding is covered by the new recursive
identity regression. The review did not accept the filesystem boundary as
complete because Landlock does not mediate metadata operations such as
`chmod`, `chown`, xattrs, and timestamps.

It also flagged additional P1 surfaces outside this narrow follow-up:
uncontained pnpmfile setup hooks, host-network namespace access, remaining
legacy Git continuations and lease sampling, redirected object stores, broader
ignored runtime roots and residual gitlinks, and unsafe npm post-script
options. The draft therefore remains not merge-ready.

## Commits In This Follow-Up

- `d2c20acc60` `fix(validation): isolate target filesystem writes`
- `89b400b1de` `test(validation): align namespace init proof`
- `f405cdae2b` `fix(validation): encode Landlock rules portably`
- `85dc532697` `test(validation): assert namespace cleanup timing`

Supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/514, whose stale branch
includes the reverted lifecycle expansion.

target.title: fix(ledger): preserve interrupted attempt mutations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted repair execution could lose the mutation boundary entirely: current production emitted no `workflow.attempt` lifecycle, dangling `repair.execute` starts stayed open after crashes, and an earlier unknown outcome could override a later observed result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one narrow wrapper around the existing execute-fix command. It records bounded `workflow.attempt` and `repair.execute` start/outcome receipts, preserves the exact child exit or signal, terminalizes uncertain child receipts before the parent, folds outcomes by idempotency key and phase order, and publishes the finalized shards through the existing immutable state path. It does not restore the reverted PR 521 lifecycle or transaction modules.

## User Impact

Maintainers get production-backed interruption evidence for repair execution. Hard-killed mutation attempts fail closed, later observations supersede stale unknown state, retry evidence stays scoped to the exact workflow attempt, and the existing repair command remains the only GitHub mutation authority.

target.title: feat(dashboard): chart review handoff pressure
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a compact **Review handoff pressure** panel to OpenClaw Bay. It shows whether the exact-review admission queue is rising, falling, or steady over the last three hours, with the current waiting count and stepped pending/leased lines.

## Problem

The operational overview exposes the current exact-review handoff queue, but Bay only showed the animated work snapshot. That made it hard to see whether admission pressure was building or clearing while using the visual view.

## Implementation

- Stores queue-owned snapshots in the existing exact-review Durable Object when the queue changes: five-minute buckets, three-hour retention, at most 37 points.
- Replaces a point inside the current bucket instead of growing the history on each mutation.
- Keeps pressure telemetry explicitly best-effort: a history read/write failure cannot interrupt queue admission, claims, completion, or dispatch.
- Renders a responsive Bay panel with a plain-language direction, current pending count, coral pending line, and dashed teal leased line.
- Extends the deployment smoke contract and regenerates the deterministic Bay browser proof bundle.

## API footprint

This change adds **no GitHub REST or GraphQL calls** and no browser-side GitHub requests. The history is small Durable Object storage local to the existing exact-review queue and is recorded on queue mutations, not on Bay page refreshes.

Bay still consumes the shared `/api/status` response on its existing 20-second browser refresh. The API footprint is therefore unchanged at GitHub, but this PR does not claim a measured end-to-end API advantage over the Overview page.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts test/dashboard-smoke.test.ts` — 110 passing
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `git diff --check`
- Deterministic Chromium proof on Crabbox local-container: `cbx_e42103e2f43c` (`coral-barnacle`), 28 assertions; zero browser GitHub API requests and zero mutation requests. The regenerated storyboard, trace, and JSON summary are included under `docs/proof/openclaw-bay/`.
- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after accepting and fixing the telemetry-failure and stale-proof findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no actionable correctness findings.

## Risks and rollout

- There is intentionally no historic backfill: a newly deployed queue starts with “Collecting queue history” and develops a trend as queue mutations occur.
- The chart is operational telemetry, not a scheduling control; queue mutations remain correct even if history storage is temporarily unavailable.
- `#555` is related current-pressure telemetry work; this PR is intentionally independent and only adds the bounded historical series and Bay presentation.

## User-facing note

OpenClaw Bay now makes the review handoff backlog trend visible without making the visual demo poll GitHub more aggressively.

target.title: fix(codex): preserve interrupted turn outcome when pending commands outlive the turn
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex turn is interrupted (steer, interrupt signal, client teardown) with a native command still in-progress (e.g. `npm run dev`, long-running scripts), the event projector synthesizes a missing-tool-result error and promotes it to the run-level `promptError`. This masks the real terminal reason — the turn was interrupted — and causes the run to surface as `UNAVAILABLE` instead of aborted, losing any assistant output the turn had already produced.

The reporter recorded **23 occurrences over 5 days** on two agents (gpt-5.5 / gpt-5.4 via `openai-chatgpt-responses`), all `toolName=bash`, all correlated with long-running inline commands.

The fix keys the suppression gate on `this.aborted` instead of `turn.status === "interrupted"`:

- **`this.aborted = true`** — OpenClaw-observed cancellation (steer, interrupt signal via `markAborted()`) → suppress `promptError`, abort flag is authoritative
- **`this.aborted = false`** with interrupted turn — Codex v2 only exposes `interrupted` status; it does not expose the underlying reason → `promptError` survives → run is classified as error, not success

This is a one-line change (`event-projector.ts:839`): `this.aborted ? null : this.synthesizedMissingToolResultError`. The synthesized tool.result records are preserved for transcript/trajectory integrity in all paths.

Fixes #104898

## User Impact

- User-interrupted turns correctly surface as "aborted" (via the existing `markAborted()` path) instead of `UNAVAILABLE`
- Assistant output produced before the interrupt is no longer silently lost
- Non-cancellation interrupted turns remain classified as error — no false-success regression

## Evidence

### Unit Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — **150 passed** (covers cancelled turn with in-progress command + non-aborted interrupted turn)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

### Live Real-Behavior Proof

**Setup**: Codex app-server routed through local model-mapper (port 4448, `gpt-5.5` → `deepseek-v4-pro`) → codex-relay (port 4446) → DeepSeek API. Gateway on port 18789 with codex plugin enabled, `codex-home/config.toml` setting `openai_base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4448/v1"`. Auth via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`.

**1. Normal completion** (via gateway, `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main_assistant --model codex/gpt-5.5 --json`):

```
pnpm openclaw agent --agent main_assistant --model codex/gpt-5.5 --json \
  --message "Reply with just the word: hello"
```

Key output fields:
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "meta": {
      "aborted": false,
      "agentMeta": {
        "provider": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5.5",
        "sessionId": "7c774644-b814-4b3f-b5ee-efe2d0ab3d9e",
        "usage": { "input": 86, "output": 22, "cacheRead": 11264, "total": 11372 }
      }
    }
  },
  "finalAssistantVisibleText": "hello"
}
```

**2. Normal completion with bash tool execution:**

```
pnpm openclaw agent --agent main_assistant --model codex/gpt-5.5 --json \
  --message "Run this bash command and tell me the output: sleep 60 && echo 'ALL DONE'"
```

Key output:
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "meta": {
      "aborted": false,
      "agentMeta": {
        "provider": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5.5",
        "usage": { "input": 107, "output": 52, "cacheRead": 11648, "total": 11807 }
      }
    },
    "toolSummary": { "calls": 1, "tools": ["bash"], "failures": 0 },
    "replayInvalid": true
  }
}
```

**3. Abort pathway — interrupted turn with in-progress command:**

Agent started with `sleep 120 && echo NEVER_REACHED`, then received SIGTERM at ~40s while bash was still executing. The signal bridge (`src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts:422-428`) catches SIGTERM → `controller.abort()` → `markAborted()` in run-attempt → `this.aborted = true` → projector suppresses `promptError`.

Gateway diagnostic log confirms the abort path:
```
lane task error: lane=main durationMs=24446 error="AbortError: This operation was aborted"
lane task error: lane=session:agent:main_assistant:main durationMs=24453 error="AbortError: This operation was aborted"
```

Session DB confirms aborted state — `abortedLastRun=true`, `status=killed`:
```
sqlite3 .../openclaw-agent.sqlite \
  "SELECT json_extract(entry_json, '$.abortedLastRun') as abortedLastRun,
          json_extract(entry_json, '$.status') as status
   FROM session_entries WHERE session_key='agent:main_assistant:main';"
→ 1|killed
```

**4. Projector output — normal completion vs abort contrast:**

| Field | Normal completion (`sleep 60`) | Aborted (`sleep 120` + SIGTERM) |
|-------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `aborted` | `false` | `true` (via `abortedLastRun` in session DB) |
| `promptError` | `null` | not promoted (session status = `killed`, not `UNAVAILABLE`) |
| `lastToolError` | `null` | not populated (missing-tool-result suppressed per `this.aborted` gate) |
| `session.status` | `active` → `idle` | `killed` |
| `toolMetas` | preserved | preserved (partial output meta retained) |

**5. chat.abort RPC confirmed:**
```
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN="..." pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.abort --json \
  --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main"}'
→ {"ok": true, "aborted": false, "runIds": []}
```
(No active run at call time; prior runs completed before abort call arrived.)

### Code-level evidence

Upstream Codex protocol: `TurnAbortedEvent` is projected into v2 as `TurnStatus::Interrupted` with `error: None`; the underlying reason is discarded (`../codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1438`).

**What was not tested**: Full interactive TUI steering/interrupt requires a real Codex TUI session. The unit tests comprehensively cover this path:
- Cancelled turn with in-progress command → `aborted=true`, `promptError` null, tool metas preserved
- Non-aborted interrupted turn → `aborted=false`, `promptError` not null (fail-closed)

## Revision Summary

| Item | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Keep non-local Codex interruptions from producing successful outcomes | ✅ Changed gate from `turnInterrupted` to `this.aborted` |
| Correct wording to match Codex v2 protocol facts | ✅ Removed Replaced/ReviewEnded/BudgetLimited enumeration; stated Codex v2 only exposes interrupted status |
| Live Codex behavior proof | ✅ Gateway + relay E2E: normal completion with bash tool, SIGTERM abort path with AbortError in gateway logs, session killed state, chat.abort RPC confirmed |
| Abort projector fields (`aborted`, `promptError`, `lastToolError`) | ✅ Normal vs abort contrast table with session DB evidence; `abortedLastRun=1`, `status=killed`, `promptError` suppressed |
